• ~haben~: From MHG ~haben~, from OHG ~habēn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~habbjan~, from Proto-Germanic *~habjaną~, from PIE *~keh₂p-~ ("to grasp, seize"). Despite the resemblance it is not related to Latin ~habēō~, but it is to ~capiō~ ("I seize") and to German ~heben~. Cognate with English ~have~, Dutch ~hebben~, Danish ~have~, Gothic ~haban~.
• ~voraus-~: The compound adverb ~vor~ ("before, in front of") + ~aus~ ("out"); see those entries for their separate histories. Together they mean "ahead, in advance." ~voraus-~ means going on ahead of others in space.

~Voraushaben~ carries the spatial lead into the abstract: to ~voraushaben~ something over someone is to have the advantage of it. The verb takes a dative of the person and an accusative of the thing.
en.vorauslaufen:
A separable compound of ~voraus-~ + ~laufen~:

• ~laufen~: From MHG ~loufen~, from OHG ~hloufan~, ~loufan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~hlaupan~, from Proto-Germanic *~hlaupaną~. A class VII strong verb. The initial ~hl-~ cluster was lost during the Old High German period. Cognate with English ~leap~ and ~lope~, Dutch ~lopen~, Danish ~løbe~.
• ~voraus-~: The compound adverb ~vor~ ("before, in front of") + ~aus~ ("out"); see those entries for their separate histories. Together they mean "ahead, in advance." ~voraus-~ means going on ahead of others in space.

~Vorauslaufen~ is the literal running out ahead in space: one runs ahead of the group and the rest follow.
en.vorausreisen:
A separable compound of ~voraus-~ + ~reisen~:

• ~reisen~: From MHG ~reisen~ ("to set out on a campaign, to travel"), from OHG ~reisōn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~raisōn~, from a form akin to Proto-Germanic *~raizijaną~ ("to cause to rise"); the root *~rīsaną~ ("to rise") also gives English ~rise~. The shift from "setting out" to "traveling" ran through the military sense: a ~Reise~ was originally a campaign.
• ~voraus-~: The compound adverb ~vor~ ("before, in front of") + ~aus~ ("out"); see those entries for their separate histories. Together they mean "ahead, in advance." ~voraus-~ means going on ahead of others in space.

~Vorausreisen~ means setting out before the others and reaching the destination first: the military origin of ~reisen~ as "setting out" still resonates.
en.vorausrennen:
A separable compound of ~voraus-~ + ~rennen~:

• ~rennen~: From a merger of two Old High German verbs: the causative ~rennan~ ("to make something run or flow"), from Proto-Germanic *~rannijaną~, and the intransitive ~rinnan~ ("to run, to flow"), from Proto-Germanic *~rinnaną~, from PIE *~h₃reyH-~ ("to undulate, churn"). A member of the Rückumlaut cohort: ~ich renne~, ~rannte~, ~gerannt~; no umlaut in the preterite. Cognate with English ~run~, Dutch ~rennen~.
• ~voraus-~: The compound adverb ~vor~ ("before, in front of") + ~aus~ ("out"); see those entries for their separate histories. Together they mean "ahead, in advance." ~voraus-~ means going on ahead of others in space.

~Vorausrennen~ picks ~rennen~ for going on ahead, stressing speed; the Rückumlaut form ~rannte voraus~ shows the mixed paradigm.
en.voraussagen:
A separable compound of ~voraus-~ + ~sagen~:

• ~sagen~: From MHG ~sagen~, from OHG ~sagēn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~saggjan~, from Proto-Germanic *~sagjaną~, ultimately from PIE *~sekʷ-~ ("to say, tell"). Cognate with English ~say~, Dutch ~zeggen~, Low German ~seggen~, Danish ~sige~, Swedish ~säga~.
• ~voraus-~: The compound adverb ~vor~ ("before, in front of") + ~aus~ ("out"); see those entries for their separate histories. Together they mean "ahead, in advance." More often it is temporal: doing something in advance, before the fact.

~Voraussagen~ is purely temporal: to state something before it happens. Beside ~vorhersagen~ it keeps to the native ~sagen~ stem where German could also say ~prognostizieren~.
en.vorausschicken:
A separable compound of ~voraus-~ + ~schicken~:

• ~schicken~: From MHG ~schicken~ ("to outfit oneself, fit in, arrange appropriately"), from OHG *~skihhen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~skikkijan~, from Proto-Germanic *~skikkijaną~ ("to order, send"), the causative of the verb underlying MHG ~geschehen~ ("to happen, rush"). The sense "to send" grew from "to make ready to go." Related to English ~chic~ (via French), ~geschickt~, and ~Schicksal~.
• ~voraus-~: The compound adverb ~vor~ ("before, in front of") + ~aus~ ("out"); see those entries for their separate histories. Together they mean "ahead, in advance." More often it is temporal: doing something in advance, before the fact.

~Vorausschicken~ has, beside the literal "to send ahead," the figurative sense of prefacing: placing a remark before the main matter.
en.voraussehen:
A separable compound of ~voraus-~ + ~sehen~:

• ~sehen~: From MHG ~sëhen~, from OHG ~sëhan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~sehwan~, from Proto-Germanic *~sehwaną~, from PIE *~sekʷ-~ ("to see, notice"). Cognate with English ~see~, Dutch ~zien~, Danish ~se~, Gothic ~saihwan~.
• ~voraus-~: The compound adverb ~vor~ ("before, in front of") + ~aus~ ("out"); see those entries for their separate histories. Together they mean "ahead, in advance." More often it is temporal: doing something in advance, before the fact.

~Voraussehen~ moves seeing into the future: to behold an event in the mind before it occurs.
en.voraussenden:
A separable compound of ~voraus-~ + ~senden~:

• ~senden~: From MHG ~senden~, from OHG ~senten~, from Proto-West Germanic *~sandijan~, from Proto-Germanic *~sandijaną~, from PIE *~sont-eye-~, a causative of *~sent-~ ("to walk, travel"), originally "to cause to go." It has a double Präteritum: ~sendete~ for broadcasting, ~sandte~ (a Rückumlaut form) for sending a letter. Cognate with English ~send~, Dutch ~zenden~, Gothic ~sandjan~.
• ~voraus-~: The compound adverb ~vor~ ("before, in front of") + ~aus~ ("out"); see those entries for their separate histories. Together they mean "ahead, in advance." ~voraus-~ means going on ahead of others in space.

~Voraussenden~ means dispatching someone or something ahead so that it arrives first; the stem ~senden~ is loftier than ~schicken~.
en.voraussetzen:
Compound of ~voraus-~ + ~setzen~:

• ~setzen~: From MHG ~setzen~, from OHG ~sezzen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~sattjan~, a causative from Proto-Germanic *~satjaną~ ("to set"), from PIE *~sed-~ ("to sit"). Cognate with English ~set~ and Dutch ~zetten~.
• ~voraus-~: Compound prefix from ~vor~ ("before, forward," from PIE *~preh₂~) + ~aus~ ("out," from PIE *~úd~). Together, ~voraus~ means "ahead, in advance."

~Voraussetzen~ means "to presuppose, to assume as given", literally "to set out ahead," placing a condition before the argument. The noun ~Voraussetzung~ ("prerequisite, precondition") is ubiquitous in academic and bureaucratic German. The PIE root *~sed-~ ("to sit") is one of the most productive roots in the Indo-European family, generating Latin ~sedēre~ ("to sit"), English ~sit~, ~set~, ~seat~, ~settle~, ~saddle~, ~cathedral~ (via Greek ~kathedra~, "seat"), and ~nest~ (from *~ni-sd-os~, "where one sits down").
en.vorauszahlen:
A separable compound of ~voraus-~ + ~zahlen~:

• ~zahlen~: From MHG ~zaln~, ~zalen~, from OHG ~zalōn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~talōn~, from Proto-Germanic *~talōną~ ("to tell, recount; to count, reckon"). ~Zahlen~ and ~zählen~ are siblings from the same root: payment requires counting out the correct amount. Cognate with English ~tale~ and ~tell~, Dutch ~betalen~, Swedish ~tala~.
• ~voraus-~: The compound adverb ~vor~ ("before, in front of") + ~aus~ ("out"); see those entries for their separate histories. Together they mean "ahead, in advance." More often it is temporal: doing something in advance, before the fact.

~Vorauszahlen~ is temporal: handing over the sum before the service is rendered. The tie between ~zahlen~ and ~zählen~, counting out the amount, is especially close here.
en.vorbauen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~bauen~:

• ~bauen~: From MHG ~būwen~, from OHG ~būan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~būan~, from Proto-Germanic *~būaną~ ("to dwell, reside"), from PIE *~bʰuH-~ ("to be, become, grow"); one builds where one lives. Cognate with English ~be~, ~bower~ ("dwelling"), ~neighbor~ ("near-dweller"), Dutch ~bouwen~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys doing something in advance, before the need arises.

~Vorbauen~ means both fabricating a component in advance and, proverbially, taking timely precautions: one who ~vorbaut~ is guarded against future harm.
en.vorbehalten:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~be-~ + ~halten~:

• ~halten~: From MHG ~halten~, from OHG ~haltan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~haldan~, from Proto-Germanic *~haldaną~. Cognate with English ~hold~, Dutch ~houden~, Low German ~holden~, Danish ~holde~, Icelandic ~halda~, Swedish ~hålla~.
• ~be-~: From MHG ~be-~, from OHG ~bi-~, from Proto-West Germanic *~bi-~, from Proto-Germanic *~bi-~ ("by, at, around"), from PIE *~h₁epi~ ("on, at, near"). The unstressed proclitic form of the preposition ~bei~. ~be-~ adds thoroughness or completeness to the base action.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys doing something in advance, before the need arises.

~Behalten~ has long been a fixed unit ("to keep, not give up"); ~vor-~ adds the holding-back for later: to ~vorbehalten~ oneself something is to reserve a right against future need. The verb stays strong (~vorbehalten~, not *~vorbehaltet~).
en.vorbehandeln:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~be-~ + ~handeln~:

• ~handeln~: From MHG ~handeln~, from OHG ~hantalōn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~handulōn~, a denominative verb from Proto-Germanic *~handuz~ ("hand") with the frequentative suffix *~-lōną~; the sense broadened from "to handle" to "to act, deal, trade." Cognate with English ~handle~, Dutch ~handelen~, Danish ~handle~.
• ~be-~: From MHG ~be-~, from OHG ~bi-~, from Proto-West Germanic *~bi-~, from Proto-Germanic *~bi-~ ("by, at, around"), from PIE *~h₁epi~ ("on, at, near"). The unstressed proclitic form of the preposition ~bei~. ~be-~ makes an intransitive verb transitive, directing the action at an object.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys doing something in advance, before the need arises.

~Behandeln~ turns intransitive ~handeln~ into a transitive verb; ~vor-~ places the treatment before the main one: to ~vorbehandeln~ a material before it is processed further.
en.vorbeifahren:
A separable compound of ~vorbei-~ + ~fahren~:

• ~fahren~: From MHG ~varn~, from OHG ~faran~, from Proto-West Germanic *~faran~, from Proto-Germanic *~faraną~, from PIE *~per-~ ("going, passage"). A class VI strong verb whose old sense "to go, travel" narrowed to vehicular travel; the causative ~führen~ (*~fōrijaną~) is its transitive counterpart. Cognate with English ~fare~, Dutch ~varen~, Danish ~fare~.
• ~vorbei-~: A transparent compound of ~vor~ ("before, in front") and ~bei~ ("by, near"): something passes in front of and close by, hence "past, by." Like ~dahin~ it took on a temporal sense; ~vorbei~ alone means "over, finished." ~vorbei-~ marks motion past something without stopping.

~Vorbeifahren~ is passing by in a vehicle without stopping: the particle's commonest concrete reading.
en.vorbeigehen:
A separable compound of ~vorbei-~ + ~gehen~:

• ~gehen~: From MHG ~gan~, ~gen~, from OHG ~gan~, ~gen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~gān~, from Proto-Germanic *~gāną~, from PIE *~ǵʰeh₁-~ ("to leave"). The form ~gen~ is of Bavarian origin; the ~-h-~ entered the spelling by analogy with ~sehen~. Cognate with English ~go~, Dutch ~gaan~, Low German ~gahn~, Swedish and Danish ~gå~.
• ~vorbei-~: A transparent compound of ~vor~ ("before, in front") and ~bei~ ("by, near"): something passes in front of and close by, hence "past, by." Like ~dahin~ it took on a temporal sense; ~vorbei~ alone means "over, finished." ~vorbei-~ marks motion past something without stopping.

~Vorbeigehen~ literally means walking past; figuratively, to go past something is to miss its point.
en.vorbeikommen:
A separable compound of ~vorbei-~ + ~kommen~:

• ~kommen~: From MHG ~quemen~, ~komen~, ~kumen~, from OHG ~queman~ (rarer ~cuman~, ~chuman~), from Proto-West Germanic *~kweman~, from Proto-Germanic *~kwemaną~, from PIE *~gʷem-~. Cognate with English ~come~, Low German ~kamen~, Dutch ~komen~, Danish ~komme~.
• ~vorbei-~: A transparent compound of ~vor~ ("before, in front") and ~bei~ ("by, near"): something passes in front of and close by, hence "past, by." Like ~dahin~ it took on a temporal sense; ~vorbei~ alone means "over, finished." Of a brief visit, dropping by (~vorbeikommen~, ~vorbeischauen~).

Beside the literal passing-by, ~vorbeikommen~ carries the familiar sense of a short visit: one drops in while passing.
en.vorbeilaufen:
A separable compound of ~vorbei-~ + ~laufen~:

• ~laufen~: From MHG ~loufen~, from OHG ~hloufan~, ~loufan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~hlaupan~, from Proto-Germanic *~hlaupaną~. A class VII strong verb. The initial ~hl-~ cluster was lost during the Old High German period. Cognate with English ~leap~ and ~lope~, Dutch ~lopen~, Danish ~løbe~.
• ~vorbei-~: A transparent compound of ~vor~ ("before, in front") and ~bei~ ("by, near"): something passes in front of and close by, hence "past, by." Like ~dahin~ it took on a temporal sense; ~vorbei~ alone means "over, finished." ~vorbei-~ marks motion past something without stopping.

~Vorbeilaufen~ is passing by on foot, often in haste; the particle marks motion past a point.
en.vorbeireden:
A separable compound of ~vorbei-~ + ~reden~:

• ~reden~: From MHG ~reden~, from OHG ~redōn~, ~rediōn~ ("to speak"), a denominal verb from ~reda~, ~redia~ ("speech, word, opinion"), from Proto-Germanic *~raþjǭ~ ("accountability, speech"). The shared PIE root carried the sense of organized, accountable speech. Cognate with Latin ~ratiō~ (whence English ~ratio~, ~reason~), English ~rede~ ("counsel"), and German ~Rat~.
• ~vorbei-~: A transparent compound of ~vor~ ("before, in front") and ~bei~ ("by, near"): something passes in front of and close by, hence "past, by." Like ~dahin~ it took on a temporal sense; ~vorbei~ alone means "over, finished." Of missing a target, going past rather than into it (~vorbeischießen~, ~vorbeireden~).

In ~aneinander vorbeireden~ the talk never reaches its target: people talk past rather than to one another.
en.vorbeischauen:
A separable compound of ~vorbei-~ + ~schauen~:

• ~schauen~: From MHG ~schouwen~, from OHG ~scouwōn~, from Proto-Germanic *~skawwōną~ ("to look, see, watch"), from PIE *~(s)kewh₁-~ ("to heed, look, take note of"). The same root gives English ~show~, the Germanic descendants dividing between intransitive "to look" and transitive "to make visible." The verb is characteristic of southern German, Austrian, and Swiss usage. Cognate with English ~show~, Dutch ~schouwen~.
• ~vorbei-~: A transparent compound of ~vor~ ("before, in front") and ~bei~ ("by, near"): something passes in front of and close by, hence "past, by." Like ~dahin~ it took on a temporal sense; ~vorbei~ alone means "over, finished." ~vorbei-~ marks motion past something without stopping.

~Vorbeischauen~ here means letting the gaze pass by something: to look past it.
en.vorbereiten:
From ~vor-~ + ~bereiten~, itself a double-prefix compound. ~Bereiten~ descends from Old High German ~bireitan~, formed from ~bi-~ (an ancestral form of the modern prefix ~be-~) + a verb derived from Proto-Germanic *~raidijaną~ ("to arrange, make ready").

• ~bereiten~: From MHG ~bereiten~, from OHG ~bireitan~, from the prefix ~bi-~ + a denominal verb from the Proto-Germanic adjective *~raidaz~ ("ready, arranged"), from PIE *~rēy-~ ("to arrange, prepare"). The adjective *~raidaz~ also yields the German adjective ~bereit~ ("ready, prepared") and, across the North Sea, English ~ready~, a direct cognate. Proto-Germanic *~raidijaną~ ("to arrange") is itself a denominative causative: "to make ready."
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor-~, from OHG ~fora-~, from Proto-Germanic *~fura-~, from PIE *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). The prefix adds the sense of doing something in advance, preparing before the need arises.

The double-prefix structure of ~vorbereiten~ (vor- + be- + reitan) mirrors its meaning: thorough prior preparation involves multiple stages of making ready. The OHG simplex ~reitan~ ("to make ready, to equip") (ancestor of both ~bereiten~ and English ~ready~) has no direct continuation in Modern German as a simplex; it survives only in the compound and in the adjective ~bereit~. English ~ready~ and German ~bereit~ are thus cognates meaning precisely the same thing, both descending from the same Proto-Germanic adjective *~raidaz~, while ~bereiten~ and ~vorbereiten~ are the verbal expressions of that same root applied to the act of preparation. Cognate with Dutch ~voorbereiden~, English ~ready~ (via *~raidaz~).
en.vorbestellen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~be-~ + ~stellen~:

• ~stellen~: From MHG ~stellen~, from OHG ~stellen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~stalljan~ ("to put, position"), from PIE *~stel-~ ("to place, put"). A causative weak verb, the transitive counterpart to ~stehen~ ("to stand"). Cognate with English ~stell~ ("to place, fix"), Dutch ~stellen~, Danish ~stille~, Yiddish ~shteln~.
• ~be-~: From MHG ~be-~, from OHG ~bi-~, from Proto-West Germanic *~bi-~, from Proto-Germanic *~bi-~ ("by, at, around"), from PIE *~h₁epi~ ("on, at, near"). The unstressed proclitic form of the preposition ~bei~. ~be-~ adds thoroughness or completeness to the base action.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys doing something in advance, before the need arises.

~Bestellen~ is firmly lexicalized as "to order, send for"; ~vor-~ places the order in the time before need: to ~vorbestellen~ goods before they are available.
en.vorbestimmen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~be-~ + ~stimmen~:

• ~stimmen~: From MHG ~stimmen~, from OHG *~stimmen~, a denominative of ~Stimme~ ("voice, vote": OHG ~stimma~, Proto-West Germanic *~stebnu~, Proto-Germanic *~stebnō~, from PIE *~stomen-~ "mouth, muzzle"). Hence the senses "to tune" (an instrument), "to be correct," and "to vote." Cognate with archaic English ~steven~ ("voice"), Dutch ~stem~, Gothic ~stibna~, Ancient Greek ~stóma~ ("mouth").
• ~be-~: From MHG ~be-~, from OHG ~bi-~, from Proto-West Germanic *~bi-~, from Proto-Germanic *~bi-~ ("by, at, around"), from PIE *~h₁epi~ ("on, at, near"). The unstressed proclitic form of the preposition ~bei~. ~be-~ makes an intransitive verb transitive, directing the action at an object.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys doing something in advance, before the need arises.

~Bestimmen~ (from ~stimmen~) means "to fix, decide"; ~vor-~ moves the decision into the time before: to ~vorbestimmen~ is to settle in advance, often in the sense of destiny.
en.vorbeten:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~beten~:

• ~beten~: From MHG ~beten~, from OHG ~beton~, from Proto-West Germanic *~bedon~, from Proto-Germanic *~bedan~ ("to pray, to ask"), close to *~bidjan~ ("to ask"), from PIE *~gwhedh-~ ("to ask for, beseech"). The narrowing from "ask" to "pray" is a Christianization phenomenon. Cognate with English ~bid~, Dutch ~bidden~, Danish ~bede~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys presenting or performing something for an audience.

~Vorbeten~ means reciting the prayer aloud so that the congregation prays after: a verb of presenting something before others.
en.vorbeugen:
From ~vor-~ + ~beugen~. Compound of:

• ~beugen~: From MHG ~böugen~, from OHG ~bougen~, from Proto-Germanic *~baugijaną~, a causative of *~beuganą~ ("to bow, bend"), from PIE *~bʰewgʰ-~ ("to bend, bow").
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor-~, ~vür-~, from OHG ~fora-~, from Proto-Germanic *~fura-~, from PIE *~preh₂~ ("before, in front"). As a verbal prefix, it indicates doing something in advance.

The literal meaning is "to bend forward" (as when bowing), but the figurative sense "to prevent, forestall" (bending events away from their course before they arrive) became the primary meaning. The English idiom "to bow before" captures a similar spatial metaphor. The related strong verb ~biegen~ ("to bend") shares the same PIE root *~bʰewgʰ-~, which also gave English ~bow~ and ~elbow~ (literally "arm-bend"). In early modern German, ~beugen~ and ~biegen~ nearly merged entirely; grammarians later re-separated them, assigning ~beugen~ to figurative and ~biegen~ to physical bending.
en.vorbilden:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~bilden~:

• ~bilden~: From MHG ~bilden~, a merger of two Old High German verbs: ~biliden~ ("to form into an image"), from Proto-West Germanic *~biliþijan~, and ~bilidōn~ ("to copy, represent"), from *~biliþōn~; both from the noun *~biliþī~ (whence ~Bild~), whose pre-Germanic origin is obscure, with no secure PIE etymology. Cognate with Dutch ~beelden~, Swedish ~bilda~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys doing something in advance, before the need arises.

~Vorbilden~ ties to ~Vorbild~ ("model, prototype"): to shape something as a model or to prefigure it typologically, as in the Luther passage where the parable ~vorbildet~ the kingdom of God.
en.vorbringen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~bringen~:

• ~bringen~: From MHG ~bringen~, from OHG ~bringan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~bringan~, from Proto-Germanic *~bringaną~, probably from pre-Germanic *~bʰrenk-~, a compound root from PIE *~bʰer-~ ("to carry") + *~h₁nek-~ ("to bring"). Mixed conjugation: ~brachte~ pairs the vowel change ~i~ > ~a~ with a weak dental suffix. Cognate with English ~bring~, Dutch ~brengen~, Gothic ~briggan~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

~Vorbringen~ has narrowed from the spatial "to bring forward" to the stating of a matter: to ~vorbringen~ a motion, an objection, an opinion.
en.vordenken:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~denken~:

• ~denken~: From MHG ~denken~, from OHG ~denken~, from Proto-West Germanic *~þankijan~, from Proto-Germanic *~þankijaną~, from PIE *~teng-~ ("to think, feel"). A mixed-conjugation verb of the Rückumlaut cohort: ~dachte~ pairs the vowel change ~e~ > ~a~ with a weak dental suffix and ~k~ > ~ch~. Cognate with English ~think~, Dutch ~denken~, Icelandic ~þekkja~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys doing something in advance, before the need arises.

~Vordenken~ means anticipating a thought, playing out future situations in the mind; the mixed form ~vordachte~ shows the Rückumlaut paradigm.
en.vordringen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~dringen~:

• ~dringen~: From MHG ~dringen~, from OHG ~dringan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~þringwan~, from Proto-Germanic *~þrinhwaną~, from PIE *~trenkʷ-~ ("to beat, hew, press"). A class III strong verb (~dringen~, ~drang~, ~gedrungen~); its causative ~drängen~ carries the expected umlaut. Cognate with dialectal English ~thring~ ("to press") and English ~throng~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

~Vordringen~ is a forceful pressing forward into a space: into terrain, into a court of appeal, into a realization; the stem ~dringen~ carries the sense of pushing.
en.vorenthalten:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~ent-~ + ~halten~:

• ~halten~: From MHG ~halten~, from OHG ~haltan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~haldan~, from Proto-Germanic *~haldaną~. Cognate with English ~hold~, Dutch ~houden~, Low German ~holden~, Danish ~holde~, Icelandic ~halda~, Swedish ~hålla~.
• ~ent-~: From MHG ~ent-~, from OHG ~int-~, ~ant-~, from Proto-West Germanic *~and-~, from Proto-Germanic *~anda-~ ("against, facing, away"), from PIE *~h₂ent-~ ("face, forehead, front"). Cognate with English ~answer~, whose first element is the same morpheme. ~ent-~ conveys removal, taking away, or separation.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

"Vorenthalten" fuses the image of holding-before or holding-back with ~ent-~ into the meaning of keeping from someone what is owed to them; the compound is heavily lexicalized and no longer transparently derivable from its parts.
en.vorfahren:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~fahren~:

• ~fahren~: From MHG ~varn~, from OHG ~faran~, from Proto-West Germanic *~faran~, from Proto-Germanic *~faraną~, from PIE *~per-~ ("going, passage"). A class VI strong verb whose old sense "to go, travel" narrowed to vehicular travel; the causative ~führen~ (*~fōrijaną~) is its transitive counterpart. Cognate with English ~fare~, Dutch ~varen~, Danish ~fare~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

Literally "to drive forward": the compound denotes bringing a vehicle up to an entrance and, in traffic, pulling ahead of others.
en.vorfinden:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~finden~:

• ~finden~: From MHG ~vinden~, from OHG ~findan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~finþan~, from Proto-Germanic *~finþaną~, from PIE *~pent-~ ("to go, pass; path, bridge"). The development from "to go, pass" to "to find" parallels shifts in Slavic. Cognate with English ~find~, Dutch ~vinden~, Low German ~finden~, Danish ~finde~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

"Vorfinden" is to come upon something already in place: the focus falls on what is already present, not on an active search.
en.vorfordern:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~fordern~:

• ~fordern~: From MHG ~vodern~, ~vordern~, from OHG ~fordarōn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~forþ(a)rōn~, from Proto-Germanic *~furþą~, from PIE *~pŕ̥-to-~, from *~per-~ ("forward, through"); "to push forward" became "to advance a claim." Not to be confused with umlauted ~fördern~ from the same root. Cognate with English ~forth~, ~forward~ and ~further~, Dutch ~vorderen~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

The compound denotes calling a person before an official or authority; today it is largely displaced by ~vorladen~.
en.vorführen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~führen~:

• ~führen~: From MHG ~vüeren~, from OHG ~fuoren~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fōrijan~, from Proto-Germanic *~fōrijaną~, the causative of *~faraną~ ("to go, travel"), from PIE *~per-~ ("going, passage"). To ~führen~ is thus "to make go," the transitive counterpart of strong ~fahren~. Cognate with Dutch ~voeren~, English ~fare~ (from the base verb).
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys presenting or performing something for an audience.

"Vorführen" is to present something to an audience: a skill, a device, a film; distinct from the legal sense of bringing someone before a judge.
en.vorgeben:
From ~vor-~ + ~geben~. Cognate with Middle Low German ~vȫrgēven~ ("to pretend"), English ~foregive~, and Danish ~foregive~ ("to pretend"). Compound of:

• ~geben~: From MHG ~gëben~, from OHG ~gëban~ ("to bring, reach, give"), from Proto-West Germanic *~geban~, from Proto-Germanic *~gebaną~, from PIE *~gʰebʰ-~ ("to give").
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor-~, ~vür-~, from OHG ~fora-~, from Proto-Germanic *~fura-~, from PIE *~preh₂~ ("before, in front"). As a verbal prefix, it indicates putting something forward or in advance.

The primary modern meaning "to claim, pretend" (literally "to give forth, put forward") reflects the idea of presenting something that may not be genuine. Middle Low German ~vȫrgēven~ and Danish ~foregive~ developed the same "pretend" sense independently, suggesting this metaphor was widespread across the Germanic-speaking world. The secondary meaning "to set, dictate" (as in ~das Tempo vorgeben~, "to set the pace") preserves the more literal sense of putting something forward as a standard.
en.vorgehen:
Compound of ~vor-~ + ~gehen~:

• ~gehen~: From MHG ~gan~, ~gen~, from OHG ~gan~, ~gen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~gan~, from Proto-Germanic *~ganan~, from PIE *~gheh₁-~ ("to leave, to go"). Cognate with Dutch ~gaan~, Swedish ~ga~, Danish ~ga~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor(e)-~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~fura~ ("before"), from PIE *~preh₂~ ("before, in front"). This prefix adds a sense of moving forward or preceding.

The PIE root *~gheh₁-~ is notably not the source of English ~go~, which comes instead from a different root; the German-English cognate pair here is ~gehen~/~gang~ (as in English ~gang~, originally "a going, a way"). The form ~gen~ (with ~e~ instead of ~a~) is of Bavarian origin but became standard. The spelling with ~-h-~ was introduced by analogy with ~sehen~, where it had become silent but was kept in writing. As a separable verb, ~vorgehen~ means "to proceed, to go ahead, to take action," but also "to go on, to be happening" (~Was geht hier vor?~, "What is going on here?") and even "to be fast" when referring to a clock. This polysemy makes it one of the most contextually versatile ~vor-~ compounds.
en.vorgreifen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~greifen~:

• ~greifen~: From MHG ~grîfen~, from OHG ~grīfan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~grīpan~, from Proto-Germanic *~grīpaną~, from PIE *~gʰreyb-~ ("to grab, grasp"). A class I strong verb (~greift~, ~griff~, ~gegriffen~), like ~reiten~ and ~schneiden~. Cognate with English ~gripe~, Dutch ~grijpen~, Low German ~griepen~, Old Norse ~gripa~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

Literally "to reach forward"; usually figurative: to ~vorgreifen~ a matter is to get ahead of it prematurely, anticipating what is not yet due.
en.vorhaben:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~haben~:

• ~haben~: From MHG ~haben~, from OHG ~habēn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~habbjan~, from Proto-Germanic *~habjaną~, from PIE *~keh₂p-~ ("to grasp, seize"). Despite the resemblance it is not related to Latin ~habēō~, but it is to ~capiō~ ("I seize") and to German ~heben~. Cognate with English ~have~, Dutch ~hebben~, Danish ~have~, Gothic ~haban~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

To ~vorhaben~ something is to have it before oneself as an intention; the noun ~das Vorhaben~ ("undertaking, project") is the reified form of the same image.
en.vorhalten:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~halten~:

• ~halten~: From MHG ~halten~, from OHG ~haltan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~haldan~, from Proto-Germanic *~haldaną~. Cognate with English ~hold~, Dutch ~houden~, Low German ~holden~, Danish ~holde~, Icelandic ~halda~, Swedish ~hålla~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

"Vorhalten" is literally to hold something in front of someone (a mirror, a cloth) and figuratively to reproach them with something; both readings share the image of holding-before.
en.vorherberechnen:
A separable compound of ~vorher-~ + ~be-~ + ~rechnen~:

• ~rechnen~: From MHG ~rechenen~, from OHG ~rehhanōn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~rekanōn~ ("to count, explain"), from PIE *~h₃reǵ-~ ("to make straight or right"), the same root as German ~recht~ and Latin ~rectus~. Cognate with English ~reckon~, Dutch ~rekenen~, Low German ~rekenen~, Danish ~regne~.
• ~be-~: From MHG ~be-~, from OHG ~bi-~, from Proto-West Germanic *~bi-~, from Proto-Germanic *~bi-~ ("by, at, around"), from PIE *~h₁epi~ ("on, at, near"). The unstressed proclitic form of the preposition ~bei~. ~be-~ adds thoroughness or completeness to the base action.
• ~vorher-~: Transparently ~vor~ ("before") + ~her~, the deictic adverb of motion toward the speaker and, temporally, from an earlier point. The compound means "beforehand, in advance," and in verbal compounds it places an action prior to some reference point: ~vorhersagen~ ("to predict"), ~vorhersehen~ ("to foresee"). See the entries for ~vor-~ and ~her-~ for the component histories. The sense of ~vorher-~ here is: beforehand, in advance, ahead of time.

The compound sets ~vorher-~ before ~berechnen~: to work out a quantity by calculation in advance, before it comes to pass.
en.vorherbestimmen:
A separable compound of ~vorher-~ + ~be-~ + ~stimmen~:

• ~stimmen~: From MHG ~stimmen~, from OHG *~stimmen~, a denominative of ~Stimme~ ("voice, vote": OHG ~stimma~, Proto-West Germanic *~stebnu~, Proto-Germanic *~stebnō~, from PIE *~stomen-~ "mouth, muzzle"). Hence the senses "to tune" (an instrument), "to be correct," and "to vote." Cognate with archaic English ~steven~ ("voice"), Dutch ~stem~, Gothic ~stibna~, Ancient Greek ~stóma~ ("mouth").
• ~be-~: From MHG ~be-~, from OHG ~bi-~, from Proto-West Germanic *~bi-~, from Proto-Germanic *~bi-~ ("by, at, around"), from PIE *~h₁epi~ ("on, at, near"). The unstressed proclitic form of the preposition ~bei~. ~be-~ adds thoroughness or completeness to the base action.
• ~vorher-~: Transparently ~vor~ ("before") + ~her~, the deictic adverb of motion toward the speaker and, temporally, from an earlier point. The compound means "beforehand, in advance," and in verbal compounds it places an action prior to some reference point: ~vorhersagen~ ("to predict"), ~vorhersehen~ ("to foresee"). See the entries for ~vor-~ and ~her-~ for the component histories. The sense of ~vorher-~ here is: beforehand, in advance, ahead of time.

~Vorher-~ before ~bestimmen~ yields "to fix in advance"; in theological use it is the German term for predestination.
en.vorhergehen:
A separable compound of ~vorher-~ + ~gehen~:

• ~gehen~: From MHG ~gan~, ~gen~, from OHG ~gan~, ~gen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~gān~, from Proto-Germanic *~gāną~, from PIE *~ǵʰeh₁-~ ("to leave"). The form ~gen~ is of Bavarian origin; the ~-h-~ entered the spelling by analogy with ~sehen~. Cognate with English ~go~, Dutch ~gaan~, Low German ~gahn~, Swedish and Danish ~gå~.
• ~vorher-~: Transparently ~vor~ ("before") + ~her~, the deictic adverb of motion toward the speaker and, temporally, from an earlier point. The compound means "beforehand, in advance," and in verbal compounds it places an action prior to some reference point: ~vorhersagen~ ("to predict"), ~vorhersehen~ ("to foresee"). See the entries for ~vor-~ and ~her-~ for the component histories. The sense of ~vorher-~ here is: prior to some reference point in the sequence of events.

"Vorhergehen" is to lie before something else in time or space; the participle ~vorhergehend~ serves as the adjective "previous, preceding."
en.vorherrschen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~herrschen~:

• ~herrschen~: From MHG ~hērschen~, from OHG ~hērrisōn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~hairisōn~ ("to be strong, to dominate"); the form was remodeled after ~Herr~ already in MHG. ~Herr~ is originally the comparative of ~hēr~ ("grey-haired, noble"), from Proto-Germanic *~hairaz~ ("grey"). Cognate with English ~hoar~ and ~hoary~, Dutch ~heer~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys precedence: putting one thing ahead of another.

"Vorherrschen" is to be the governing one among several: a color, a mood, an opinion predominates; the participle ~vorherrschend~ means "prevailing."
en.vorhersagen:
A separable compound of ~vorher-~ + ~sagen~:

• ~sagen~: From MHG ~sagen~, from OHG ~sagēn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~saggjan~, from Proto-Germanic *~sagjaną~, ultimately from PIE *~sekʷ-~ ("to say, tell"). Cognate with English ~say~, Dutch ~zeggen~, Low German ~seggen~, Danish ~sige~, Swedish ~säga~.
• ~vorher-~: Transparently ~vor~ ("before") + ~her~, the deictic adverb of motion toward the speaker and, temporally, from an earlier point. The compound means "beforehand, in advance," and in verbal compounds it places an action prior to some reference point: ~vorhersagen~ ("to predict"), ~vorhersehen~ ("to foresee"). See the entries for ~vor-~ and ~her-~ for the component histories. The sense of ~vorher-~ here is: anticipating what is still to come.

"Vorhersagen" is to state a future event in advance; ~die Vorhersage~ is the result, especially the weather forecast.
en.vorhersehen:
A separable compound of ~vorher-~ + ~sehen~:

• ~sehen~: From MHG ~sëhen~, from OHG ~sëhan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~sehwan~, from Proto-Germanic *~sehwaną~, from PIE *~sekʷ-~ ("to see, notice"). Cognate with English ~see~, Dutch ~zien~, Danish ~se~, Gothic ~saihwan~.
• ~vorher-~: Transparently ~vor~ ("before") + ~her~, the deictic adverb of motion toward the speaker and, temporally, from an earlier point. The compound means "beforehand, in advance," and in verbal compounds it places an action prior to some reference point: ~vorhersagen~ ("to predict"), ~vorhersehen~ ("to foresee"). See the entries for ~vor-~ and ~her-~ for the component histories. The sense of ~vorher-~ here is: anticipating what is still to come.

"Vorhersehen" is to glimpse a future event in the mind before it happens: sight, not speech, anticipates what is coming.
en.vorhängen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~hängen~:

• ~hängen~: The merger of three OHG verbs: ~hāhan~ (strong, transitive; past ~hieng~, participle ~gehangan~), from Proto-West Germanic *~hą̄han~, from Proto-Germanic *~hanhaną~; ~hangēn~ (weak, intransitive); and the causative ~hengen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~hangijan~, from Proto-Germanic *~hangijaną~. The distinction is upheld chiefly in the past tense: intransitive ~hing~/~gehangen~ versus transitive ~hängte~/~gehängt~. Cognate with Dutch ~hangen~, English ~hang~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

"Vorhängen" is the transitive, weakly inflected ~hängen~ (~hängte vor~, ~vorgehängt~): to hang something (a curtain, a padlock) in front of something else; hence ~der Vorhang~ ("curtain") and ~das Vorhängeschloss~ ("padlock").
en.vorkehren:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~kehren~:

• ~kehren~: A homograph concealing two distinct verbs. ~Kehren~ (1) "to turn": from MHG ~kēren~, from OHG ~kēran~, ~chēren~, from Proto-Germanic *~kairijaną~ or *~kausijaną~, of uncertain PIE origin, possibly connected to *~gers-~ ("to twist, bend, turn"). ~Kehren~ (2) "to sweep": from MHG ~kern~, ~keren~, from OHG ~kerian~, ~cherian~, from Proto-Germanic *~karjaną~ ("to scrape, scratch"), from PIE *~ger-~ ("to scrape"). Etymologically unrelated, merged through phonological convergence.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

Here ~kehren~ is "to turn," not "to sweep": to turn something to the front, to put it on display. (Distinct, though from the same verb, is the phrase ~Vorkehrungen treffen~, "to take precautions.")
en.vorkommen:
From Middle High German ~vorekomen~, ~vurekomen~, from Old High German ~furaqueman~, ~furikweman~, from Proto-West Germanic *~forakweman~, from Proto-Germanic *~furaikwemaną~. Compound of ~vor-~ + ~kommen~:

• ~kommen~: From MHG ~komen~, from OHG ~queman~, from Proto-Germanic *~kwemaną~, from PIE *~gʷem-~ ("to come, to go").
• ~vor-~: From PIE *~preh₂~ ("before, in front"). The prefix adds a sense of coming forward, appearing before someone.

~Vorkommen~ means "to occur, to happen; to seem, to appear; to be found (in nature)." The literal sense ("to come forward, to come before") underlies all three modern meanings: what ~occurs~ comes forward into reality; what ~seems~ a certain way comes before your judgment; a mineral that ~is found~ in rock comes before the prospector. The impersonal construction ~es kommt mir vor~ ("it seems to me") preserves the original image of something presenting itself before the speaker. The OHG form ~furaqueman~ shows the old consonant: ~qu~ (from Proto-Germanic *~kw~), which simplified to ~k~ in modern German ~kommen~ but survives in English ~come~ (from the same root). Cognate with English ~forecome~ (archaic), Dutch ~voorkomen~ ("to occur; to prevent").
en.vorladen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~laden~:

• ~laden~: Two historically distinct verbs under one infinitive. ~laden~ (strong, "to load"): from MHG ~laden~, from OHG ~hladan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~hlaþan~, from Proto-Germanic *~hlaþaną~, from PIE *~kleh₂-~ ("to put, lay out"); cognate with English ~lade~ and ~laden~, Lithuanian ~klṓti~. ~laden~ (weak, "to invite, summon"): from MHG ~laden~, from OHG ~ladon~, from Proto-West Germanic *~laþōn~, from Proto-Germanic *~laþōną~, from *~laþō~ ("invitation"), from PIE *~h₂lot-eh₂~, a root found only in Germanic and Anatolian (Hittite ~halzai~).
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

"Vorladen" belongs to weak ~laden~ "to invite, summon," not to strong ~laden~ "to load," yet in modern German it has crossed into the strong inflection: ~lud vor~, ~vorgeladen~; its meaning comes from the one verb, its conjugation from the other.
en.vorlaufen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~laufen~:

• ~laufen~: From MHG ~loufen~, from OHG ~hloufan~, ~loufan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~hlaupan~, from Proto-Germanic *~hlaupaną~. A class VII strong verb. The initial ~hl-~ cluster was lost during the Old High German period. Cognate with English ~leap~ and ~lope~, Dutch ~lopen~, Danish ~løbe~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

"Vorlaufen" is to run some distance ahead of the others; as a verb of motion it forms its perfect with ~sein~ (~ist vorgelaufen~).
en.vorlegen:
From ~vor-~ + ~legen~. Compound of:

• ~legen~: From MHG ~legen~, from OHG ~leggen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~laggjan~, from Proto-Germanic *~lagjaną~, from PIE *~logʰéyeti~. This is the causative of *~legʰ-~ ("to lie down"), literally "to cause to lie," hence "to lay, to place." Cognate with English ~lay~, Dutch ~leggen~, Danish ~lægge~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor-~, ~vür-~, from OHG ~fora-~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~preh₂~ ("before, in front"). As a verbal prefix, it conveys the sense of placing something forward or presenting it.

The semantic range of ~vorlegen~ ("to present, to submit, to serve (food), to put on (a lock)") all derives from the core image of placing something ~before~ someone. One ~legt~ a document ~vor~ (presents it), ~legt~ food ~vor~ (serves it), or ~legt~ a padlock ~vor~ (puts it on). The noun ~Vorlage~ ("template, submission, model") is the corresponding nominalization, widely used in legislative contexts (~Gesetzesvorlage~ = "draft bill") and in soccer (~eine Vorlage geben~ = "to deliver an assist"). The causative relationship between ~legen~ ("to lay") and ~liegen~ ("to lie") (one makes something do what the other describes) is a textbook example of Germanic ablaut morphology.
en.vorleisten:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~leisten~:

• ~leisten~: From MHG ~leisten~, from OHG ~leisten~, from Proto-West Germanic *~laistijan~, from Proto-Germanic *~laistijaną~, a denominative of *~laistaz~ ("track, footprint"), from PIE *~leys-~ ("to track; furrow, trail"). Originally "to track, follow," then "to perform, accomplish." Cognate with English ~last~ (OE ~lǣstan~), Old Saxon ~lēstian~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys doing something in advance, before the need arises.

"Vorleisten" is to render a performance before the counter-performance follows: in law, the advance performance of one contracting party.
en.vorlesen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~lesen~:

• ~lesen~: From MHG ~lësen~, from OHG ~lësan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~lesan~, from Proto-Germanic *~lesaną~ ("to gather"), from PIE *~les-~ ("to gather"). The shift from "to gather" to "to read", paralleled in Latin ~legō~ ("I gather; I read"), construes reading as gathering letters. Cognate with Dutch ~lezen~, English ~lease~ (archaic).
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys presenting or performing something for an audience.

"Vorlesen" is to present a text aloud for listeners; ~die Vorlesung~ (a university "lecture") is the same act institutionalized.
en.vorliebnehmen:
A separable compound of ~vorlieb-~ + ~nehmen~:

• ~nehmen~: From MHG ~nëmen~, from OHG ~nëman~, from Proto-West Germanic *~neman~, from Proto-Germanic *~nemaną~, from PIE *~nem-~ ("to give or take one's due"). A class IV strong verb. Cognate with Dutch ~nemen~, English ~nim~ ("to take, filch"), Danish ~nemme~.
• ~vorlieb-~: A univerbation of the preposition ~vor~ (beside the variant ~für~) with ~lieb~ in the accusative neuter, attested from the 16th century: ~vorlieb nehmen~ is "to take [a thing] for agreeable", hence to make do with it. ~Lieb~ is the ordinary adjective "dear, agreeable", cognate with English ~lief~ (as in ~I would as lief~) and with ~love~. The phrase has frozen solid: ~vorlieb~ occurs nowhere else, and the older variant ~fürliebnehmen~ is now archaic. The sense of ~vorlieb-~ here is in ~vorliebnehmen~: to make do with, to settle for, to content oneself with.

The verb always governs ~mit~ and a dative (~mit etwas vorliebnehmen~) and survives today almost only in this one fixed collocation.
en.vorliegen:
Equivalent to ~vor-~ + ~liegen~:

• ~liegen~: From MHG ~ligen~, from OHG ~liggen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~liggjan~, from Proto-Germanic *~ligjaną~, from PIE *~legʰ-~ ("to lie down").
• ~vor-~: From PIE *~preh₂~ ("before, in front"). The prefix adds the sense of being present or existing before someone.

~Vorliegen~ means "to be present, to exist, to be available", it is impersonal and formal, used especially in bureaucratic, legal, and scientific contexts: ~Es liegt ein Fehler vor~ ("An error exists"), ~Die Ergebnisse liegen vor~ ("The results are available"). The physical image is of something lying before you: laid out for inspection. The derived noun ~Vorlage~ ("template, draft, original") preserves the concrete sense of a document laid out in front of someone for reference. The past participle ~vorliegend~ functions as an adjective meaning "present, at hand" (~der vorliegende Fall~, "the case at hand"), making it one of the most common participial adjectives in formal German prose.
en.vorlügen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~lügen~:

• ~lügen~: From MHG ~liegen~, from OHG ~liogan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~leugan~, from Proto-Germanic *~leuganą~, from PIE *~lewgʰ-~ ("to lie, swear falsely"). A class II strong verb (~lügen~, ~log~, ~gelogen~); the ~ü~ is late, taken from the noun ~Lüge~ to keep the verb from colliding with ~liegen~. Cognate with English ~lie~, Gothic ~liugan~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys presenting or performing something for an audience.

"Vorlügen" is to lie to someone's face; the prefix aims the lie at a listener to whom it is served up.
en.vormachen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~machen~:

• ~machen~: From MHG ~machen~, from OHG ~mahhōn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~makōn~, from PIE *~mag-~ ("to knead, mix, make"). Cognate with Dutch ~maken~, Low German ~maken~, English ~make~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys presenting or performing something for an audience.

"Vormachen" has two readings: to ~vormachen~ someone something is partly to demonstrate it for them to copy, partly to deceive them with a pretense, both "before" someone, with or without deception.
en.vormerken:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~merken~:

• ~merken~: From MHG ~merken~, from OHG ~merchen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~markijan~, from Proto-Germanic *~markijaną~ ("to mark, notice"), a denominal verb from *~marką~ ("mark, sign"). To notice something is etymologically to leave a mental mark on it. Cognate with English ~mark~ (and ~remark~), Icelandic ~merkja~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys doing something in advance, before the need arises.

"Vormerken" is to note or reserve something in advance so it is not overlooked: to ~vormerken~ an appointment for oneself.
en.vornehmen:
~Vor-~ + ~nehmen~. Compound of ~vor-~ + ~nehmen~:

• ~nehmen~: From MHG ~nëmen~, from OHG ~nëman~, from Proto-West Germanic *~neman~, from Proto-Germanic *~nemaną~, from PIE *~nem-~ ("to give or take one's due").
• ~vor-~: From PIE *~preh₂~ ("before, in front"). The prefix adds the sense of forward projection or undertaking something in advance.

~Vornehmen~ means "to undertake, to intend, to resolve to do", literally "to take forward." The reflexive ~sich vornehmen~ ("to make up one's mind to do something, to set oneself a task") is ubiquitous in everyday speech. The PIE root *~nem-~ also underlies ~nehmen~ and preserves the sense of taking one's due in the idea of taking on a task or intention. A related semantic neighbor is the adjective ~vornehm~ ("distinguished, refined, upper-class"), which derives from the same compound but traveled a different path: "taking forward" came to mean "foremost in rank," hence distinguished. English ~nim~ ("to pilfer, take") is a direct cognate of ~nehmen~, now mostly archaic outside of card-game contexts. Cognate with Dutch ~voornemen~.
en.vorrücken:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~rücken~:

• ~rücken~: From MHG ~rücken~, from OHG ~rucchen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~rukkijan~. The verb means "to move, to shift" and is the base of ~verrückt~ ("crazy," literally "shifted, displaced"); the noun ~Rücken~ ("back") is etymologically a separate word. Cognate with English ~rock~, Old Norse ~rykkja~, Old English ~roccian~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

"Vorrücken" is to move forward step by step: troops, clock hands, a game piece advance; a verb of motion taking ~sein~ (~ist vorgerückt~).
en.vorsagen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~sagen~:

• ~sagen~: From MHG ~sagen~, from OHG ~sagēn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~saggjan~, from Proto-Germanic *~sagjaną~, ultimately from PIE *~sekʷ-~ ("to say, tell"). Cognate with English ~say~, Dutch ~zeggen~, Low German ~seggen~, Danish ~sige~, Swedish ~säga~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys presenting or performing something for an audience.

To ~vorsagen~ is to speak the words quietly for someone else to repeat back: in school, the surreptitious prompting of a classmate.
en.vorschieben:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~schieben~:

• ~schieben~: From MHG ~schieben~, from OHG ~skioban~, from Proto-West Germanic *~skeuban~, from Proto-Germanic *~skeubaną~, from PIE *~skewbʰ-~ ("to push, to shove, to thrust"). A class II strong verb (~schieben~, ~schob~, ~geschoben~). Cognate with English ~shove~, Dutch ~schuiven~, Danish ~skubbe~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

Literally one pushes something to the front; the idiom ~einem Ding einen Riegel vorschieben~ ("to bolt a thing shut") has grown from it the figurative sense "to put a stop to a matter."
en.vorschießen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~schießen~:

• ~schießen~: From MHG ~schiezen~, from OHG ~sciozan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~skeotan~, from Proto-Germanic *~skeutaną~ ("to shoot, to shove"), possibly from PIE *~(s)kewd-~ ("to throw, shoot, pursue"). A class II strong verb (~schießen~, ~schoss~, ~geschossen~). Cognate with English ~shoot~, Dutch ~schieten~, Old Norse ~skjóta~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

Beside the spatial "to dart forward," ~vorschießen~ carries the commercial sense of advancing someone money before it is due.
en.vorschlagen:
Compound of ~vor-~ + ~schlagen~:

• ~schlagen~: From MHG ~slahen~ (the modern ~-g-~ was inserted by analogy with past forms and the noun ~Schlag~), from OHG ~slahan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~slahan~, from Proto-Germanic *~slahaną~ ("to strike, hit"). Cognate with Dutch ~slaan~, English ~slay~ and ~slog~, Danish ~slå~, and Swedish ~slå~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor-~, from OHG ~fora-~, from Proto-Germanic *~fura-~, from PIE *~preh₂~ ("before, in front"). This prefix adds the sense of putting something "forward" or "before" others.

The compound literally means "to strike before" someone, as in laying a suggestion in front of them for consideration. This metaphor of "striking" or "hitting upon" an idea is shared across languages: English uses ~strike~ in "it struck me" and ~hit~ in "he hit upon an idea." The noun ~Vorschlag~ ("proposal, suggestion") is one of those satisfying German compounds that wears its etymology on its sleeve. The base verb ~schlagen~ shows an interesting case of ~grammatischer Wechsel~ (Verner's Law alternation): the original ~h~ in OHG ~slahan~ alternated with ~g~ in certain forms, and the ~g~ eventually won out in the infinitive. English ~slay~ preserves the older consonant pattern.
en.vorschreiben:
From ~vor-~ + ~schreiben~. Compound of:

• ~schreiben~: From MHG ~schrīben~, from OHG ~scrīban~, from Proto-West Germanic *~skrīban~ ("to write"), borrowed from Latin ~scrībō~ ("I write, scratch, draw"), from PIE *~(s)kreybʰ-~ ("to scratch, carve").
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor-~, ~vür-~, from OHG ~fora-~, from Proto-Germanic *~fura-~, from PIE *~preh₂~ ("before, in front"). As a verbal prefix, it indicates doing something in advance or setting something out beforehand.

The meaning "to prescribe, dictate, stipulate" comes from writing down rules in advance, what is ~vorgeschrieben~ has been "pre-written" and therefore mandated. English ~prescribe~ follows exactly the same logic through Latin ~praescrībere~ ("to write before"), using the Latin equivalent of ~vor-~ (namely ~prae-~) with the Latin source verb of ~schreiben~. The Germanic adoption of Latin ~scrībō~ likely occurred during the Roman occupation of the Rhineland, when writing was introduced to the Germanic peoples. Before this borrowing, the native Germanic word for scratching runes was *~wrītaną~, preserved in English ~write~.
en.vorschützen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~schützen~:

• ~schützen~: From late MHG ~schützen~ ("to protect"), attested only from around 1300 and debated in origin: either from the root of ~schießen~, from Proto-Germanic *~skeutaną~, from PIE *~(s)kewd-~ ("to advance, propel"), sense "to advance a barrier"; or from ~schütten~, from Proto-Germanic *~skudjaną~, from PIE *~(s)kewt-~ ("to shake, jolt"), sense "to pile up a protective wall." Cognate with Dutch ~schutten~ ("to dam, pen in").
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

Here the spatial sense has faded: to ~vorschützen~ something is to push a pretext in front of one's true reasons, that is, to feign it.
en.vorsehen:
From Middle High German ~vorsehen~, equivalent to ~vor-~ + ~sehen~:

• ~sehen~: From MHG ~sëhen~, from OHG ~sehan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~sehwan~, from Proto-Germanic *~sehwaną~, from PIE *~sekʷ-~ ("to see, to notice").
• ~vor-~: From PIE *~preh₂~ ("before, in front"). The prefix adds the sense of looking ahead, planning, or intending.

~Vorsehen~ means "to plan, to intend, to provide for", etymologically, "to see ahead." The past participle ~vorgesehen~ ("planned, intended, designated") is ubiquitous in German bureaucratic and organizational language: ~Das Gesetz sieht Strafen vor~ ("The law provides for penalties"), ~Der Plan sieht eine Erweiterung vor~ ("The plan envisions an expansion"). The reflexive ~sich vorsehen~ means "to be careful, to watch out", to see what is coming. The derived noun ~Vorsehung~ ("providence, divine foresight") carries theological weight: God's ~Vorsehung~ is the act of seeing and planning ahead on behalf of humanity. The Latin calque ~prōvidentia~ ("foresight," from ~prō-~ + ~vidēre~, "to see before") (whence English ~providence~), mirrors the German compound exactly: both are "seeing before," one in Latin and one in Germanic. Cognate with Dutch ~voorzien~.
en.vorsetzen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~setzen~:

• ~setzen~: From MHG ~setzen~, from OHG ~sezzen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~sattjan~, from Proto-Germanic *~satjaną~ ("to set, to place down"), from PIE *~sodéyeti~, a causative derivation of *~sitjaną~ ("to sit") with the suffix *~-janą~, literally "to cause to sit." Cognate with English ~set~, Dutch ~zetten~, Yiddish ~zetsn~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

To ~vorsetzen~ is to place something before someone: to serve up a dish, or, grammatically, to place one element in front of another.
en.vorsingen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~singen~:

• ~singen~: From MHG ~singen~, from OHG ~singan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~singwan~, from Proto-Germanic *~singwaną~, from PIE *~sengʷʰ-~ ("to recite, intone, chant"), connected to Ancient Greek ~ὀμφή~ (omphḗ, "divine voice, oracle"). A class III strong verb (~singen~, ~sang~, ~gesungen~). Cognate with English ~sing~, Gothic ~𐍃𐌹𐌲𐌲𐍅𐌰𐌽~ (siggwan), Dutch ~zingen~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys presenting or performing something for an audience.

To ~vorsingen~ is to sing before listeners: whether as an audition, or so that another may sing the tune back.
en.vorsorgen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~sorgen~:

• ~sorgen~: From MHG ~sorgen~, from OHG ~sorgēn~, from Proto-Germanic *~surgāną~, a denominative verb from *~surgō~ ("worry, sorrow, care"), from PIE *~swergʰ-~ ("to watch over, worry; be ill, suffer"). The root's duality survives in ~sorgen für~ ("to care for") beside ~sich sorgen um~ ("to worry about"). Cognate with English ~sorrow~, Dutch ~zorgen~, Danish ~sørge~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys doing something in advance, before the need arises.

To ~vorsorgen~ is to provide in advance for a future need; the noun ~Vorsorge~ ("precaution") shapes terms like ~Vorsorgeuntersuchung~ ("preventive check-up").
en.vorspielen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~spielen~:

• ~spielen~: From MHG ~spil(e)n~, from OHG ~spilōn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~spilōn~, from Proto-Germanic *~spilōną~, a denominative verb from the noun *~spilą~ ("play, game, dance"); the pre-Germanic origin is uncertain. OHG ~spilōn~ was broader, covering dance and entertainment generally. Cognate with Dutch ~spelen~, Low German ~spelen~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys presenting or performing something for an audience.

To ~vorspielen~ is to play music or act before an audience, and, figuratively, to put on an act for someone.
en.vorsprechen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~sprechen~:

• ~sprechen~: From MHG ~sprëchen~, from OHG ~sprëhhan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~sprekan~, from Proto-Germanic *~sprekaną~, probably from PIE *~spregʰ-~ ("to crackle"). The sense developed from an onomatopoeic root meaning "to crackle, make noise" to "to speak." Cognate with Dutch ~spreken~, English ~speak~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys presenting or performing something for an audience.

To ~vorsprechen~ is to deliver a text before a panel: the German word for auditioning for a stage or film role.
en.vorspringen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~springen~:

• ~springen~: From OHG ~springan~, from Proto-Germanic *~springaną~, from PIE *~sprenǵʰ-~, a nasalized form of *~sperǵʰ-~ ("to move energetically, to hasten, to spring"). A class III strong verb (~springen~, ~sprang~, ~gesprungen~). Cognate with English ~spring~, Dutch ~springen~, Danish ~springe~, Greek ~spérkhō~ ("to hasten").
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

To ~vorspringen~ is to leap forward or to jut out; an element that steps out of a façade ~springt vor~ ("projects forward").
en.vorstehen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~stehen~:

• ~stehen~: From MHG ~stān~, ~stēn~, from OHG ~stān~, ~stēn~, from Proto-West Germanic *~stān~, from Proto-Germanic *~stāną~, from PIE *~steh₂-~ ("to stand"). The ~-h-~ entered the spelling by analogy with ~sehen~; the past-tense conjugations (~stand~, ~standen~) are suppletive, from Proto-West Germanic *~standan~. Cognate with Dutch ~staan~, English ~stand~, Danish ~stå~, Swedish ~stå~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

From the spatial "to stand at the front" grew the figurative ~einer Sache vorstehen~: to stand at the head of a matter, to preside over it.
en.vorstellen:
From ~vor-~ + ~stellen~. Compound of two elements:

• ~stellen~: From MHG ~stellen~, from OHG ~stellen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~stalljan~ ("to put, position"), from PIE *~stel-~ ("to place, put"). A causative weak verb, the transitive counterpart to ~stehen~ ("to stand").
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor-~, from OHG ~fora-~, from Proto-Germanic *~fura-~, from PIE *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). As a separable prefix, ~vor-~ adds a sense of forward placement or presentation.

The semantic range of ~vorstellen~ is remarkably broad: "to place in front of," "to introduce (a person)," "to imagine," and "to represent." The reflexive ~sich vorstellen~ covers both "to introduce oneself" and "to imagine", two quite different acts united by the underlying metaphor of placing something before one's mind or another person. Cognate with Dutch ~voorstellen~ ("to propose; to introduce; to imagine").
en.vorstoßen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~stoßen~:

• ~stoßen~: From MHG ~stōzen~, from OHG ~stōzan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~stautan~, from Proto-Germanic *~stautaną~, from PIE *~stówd-e-ti~, an o-grade intensive formation from *~(s)tewd-~ ("to hit, push"); the same root produced Latin ~tundere~ ("to beat, pound"). Cognate with dialectal English ~stot~ ("to bounce, ricochet"), Dutch ~stoten~, Old Norse ~stauta~ and ~steyta~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

To ~vorstoßen~ is to thrust forward: in military use, to advance into unknown or hostile territory.
en.vortragen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~tragen~:

• ~tragen~: From MHG ~tragen~, from OHG ~tragan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~dragan~, from Proto-Germanic *~draganą~ ("to draw, drag"), from PIE *~dʰregʰ-~ ("to pull, draw, drag"). A class VI strong verb whose semantic range broadened from "to drag, pull" to "to carry, bear, wear." Cognate with English ~draw~ and ~drag~, Dutch ~dragen~, Icelandic ~draga~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys presenting or performing something for an audience.

To ~vortragen~ is to present a text or matter before an audience: to deliver a speech, perform a piece of music, or, in law, to set out the facts.
en.vorverlegen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~ver-~ + ~legen~:

• ~legen~: From MHG ~legen~, from OHG ~leggen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~laggjan~, from Proto-Germanic *~lagjaną~, a causative of *~ligjaną~ ("to lie") with the suffix *~-janą~, from PIE *~logʰéyeti~. The verb is thus the causative partner of ~liegen~: to ~legen~ is to "cause to lie," i.e., to lay. Cognate with Dutch ~leggen~, English ~lay~, Danish ~lægge~.
• ~ver-~: From MHG ~ver-~, from OHG ~fir-~, ~far-~, ~fur-~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fra-~, from Proto-Germanic *~fra-~ ("away, forth"), from PIE *~per~ ("before, in front, forward"). The single modern prefix continues three distinct Proto-Germanic prefixes, *~fra-~, *~fur-~ and *~fer-~, which fell together in Old High German. ~ver-~ conveys removal or motion away, from the prefix's older spatial sense.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

To ~vorverlegen~ is to move an appointment to an earlier point: the opposite of postponing it.
en.vorwagen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~wagen~:

• ~wagen~: From MHG ~wāgen~ ("to risk, to dare"), from OHG ~wāga~ ("scales; weight") (the modern ~Waage~) from Proto-West Germanic *~wāgu~, from Proto-Germanic *~wēgō~, related to *~weganą~ ("to move, to weigh"), from PIE *~weǵʰ-~ ("to move, to transport, to carry"): to ~wagen~ is to place something on the scales. Cognate with English ~way~, ~weigh~, Dutch ~wagen~ ("to dare").
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

~Sich vorwagen~ is to venture forward despite the danger; the verb is chiefly reflexive.
en.vorwarnen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~warnen~:

• ~warnen~: From MHG ~warnen~ ("to watch over, to protect"), from OHG ~warnōn~ ("to deny, to refuse"), from Proto-West Germanic *~warnōn~, from Proto-Germanic *~warnōną~, from PIE *~wer-~ ("to heed, to perceive, to watch out for"): from refusing danger for oneself to cautioning others. Cognate with English ~warn~, Old English ~wyrnan~, Old Norse ~varna~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys doing something in advance, before the need arises.

To ~vorwarnen~ is to warn in advance, before the danger arrives.
en.vorwegnehmen:
A separable compound of ~vorweg-~ + ~nehmen~:

• ~nehmen~: From MHG ~nëmen~, from OHG ~nëman~, from Proto-West Germanic *~neman~, from Proto-Germanic *~nemaną~, from PIE *~nem-~ ("to give or take one's due"). A class IV strong verb. Cognate with Dutch ~nemen~, English ~nim~ ("to take, filch"), Danish ~nemme~.
• ~vorweg-~: The adverb ~vorweg~, ~vor~ ("before, in front") + ~weg~ ("away"), literally "forward away", hence "ahead, in advance, beforehand". It is transparently compositional; see the entries for ~vor~ and ~weg~. ~Vorwegnehmen~ is to take a thing in advance, to anticipate it, or to give away an ending. The sense of ~vorweg-~ here is in ~vorwegnehmen~: to anticipate, to pre-empt, to give away.

The verb governs an accusative object (a result, a decision, a punchline) which is thereby made known ahead of its time.
en.vorweisen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~weisen~:

• ~weisen~: From MHG ~wīsen~, from OHG ~wīsen~, from Proto-West Germanic *~wīsijan~, from Proto-Germanic *~wīsijaną~, a denominative verb from *~wīsaz~ ("wise, knowing"), from PIE *~weyd-so-s~ ("knowledgeable"), from *~weyd-~ ("to see, know"). A class I strong verb; its senses "to show, point" and "to direct, expel" both direct knowledge or attention. Cognate with English ~wise~, ~wit~, ~wizard~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys presenting or performing something for an audience.

To ~vorweisen~ is to produce something for inspection: an ID, a certificate, a credential one can point to.
en.vorwerfen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~werfen~:

• ~werfen~: From MHG ~wërfen~, from OHG ~werfan~, from Proto-West Germanic *~werpan~, from Proto-Germanic *~werpaną~, from PIE *~wergʷ-~ ("to bend, spin, warp"). A class III strong verb (~wirft~, ~warf~, ~geworfen~). Cognate with English ~warp~, Dutch ~werpen~, Old Saxon ~werpan~, Old Norse ~verpa~, Gothic ~wairpan~.
• ~vor-~: From MHG ~vor~, ~vore~, from OHG ~fora~, from Proto-West Germanic *~fura~, from Proto-Germanic *~furai~, from PIE *~pr̥h₂-éy~, a case form of the root *~preh₂-~ ("before, in front"). Cognate with English ~fore~ and ~before~, Dutch ~voor~, Gothic ~faura~, and, from the same root, Latin ~prae~ and ~prō~. The prefix conveys forward motion or position in front.

Literally one throws something down before someone; from this grew the commonest modern sense, to ~vorwerfen~ someone something in the sense of "to reproach, to hold against."
en.vorwiegen:
A separable compound of ~vor-~ + ~wiegen~:

• ~wiegen~: Two distinct verbs, both from MHG ~wigen~.
